Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter No.806B.
COS:MLM, dated June 6, 1930, and to inform you that
William D. Allen arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong
by the s.s. "Angeres" on April 11, 1930. After residing
for one night in the Navy Y.M.C.A., Szechuen Road, he
removed on April 12 to the Chinese Y.M.C.A. where he
occupied room No. 16. Soon after his arrival here,
he got into touch with several mysterious Indians,
Chinese and Japanese and visited various addresses
at which Europeans rarely call. The Indians with whom
he was in touch included an employee of the China Press
named Krappa who is known to be hostile both to the
British Government and Municipal Police. On one occasion
Krappa and Allen went together to the Sikh Gurdwara.
Allen's Chinese associates included several persons of
the student type who live in Jukong Road and in an
alleyway off Scott Road. Some of the Japanese with
whom Allen has been seen frequent the Great China
Restaurant, No. 188 Szechuen Road, and the Oriental
Hotel, Nanking Road.

On May 24 Allen left the Chinese Y.M.C.A. and
removed to the Hongkew Hotel, North Szechuen Road,
where he was joined by his wife who is believed to have
arrived in Shanghai on May 23. On June 1 Allen and

May 21, 1930

W.O. Allen arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong at 12 noon
April 11th on the s.s. "Angers." He resided for one night at
the Navy Y.M.C.A., Szechuen Road, and the following day, April
12th, removed to the Chinese Y.M.C.A., where he occupies room
No. 16.

During his stay in Shanghai it is known that he has been
in contact with an Indian named Erappa, formerly connected with
the China Press, Nanking Road, and they are known to have
visited the Indian Gurdwara, Paoshan Road on May 2nd. On that
date Allen and Erappa met two Indians (Sikhs) one of whom is
employed as a watchman at No. 10 Museum Road. Papers were passed
between them and examined after which all entered into a lively
conversation.

Allen is also connected with several Chinese students who
live in the 2nd alleyway off Scott Road. These Chinese are
probably studying at the Chinese Y.M.C.A. He has also been
frequently seen with two Chinese who reside at No. 2089 Jukong
Road. Their names, etc. are at present unknown, but enquiries
are being made with a view to establishing their identity.

On several occasions he has been seen in company with two
Japanese whom he frequently meets at the Great China Restaurant,
No. 188 Szechuen Road. These two Japanese frequent the Oriental
Hotel, Nanking Road, and are known to have met Chinese of the
student type in a Chinese Restaurant on Foochow Road. One of
the Chinese met at this restaurant speaks Japanese.

Wang Chi-Kwang (汪智廣), native of Wuhu, has also been
seen in Allen's company. This person is a graduate of the
Shanghai College and is now working there as an accountant.
He has a brother employed in the American Oriental Trading
Corporation.

Places frequented by Allen are as follows:- Navy Y.M.C.A.,
Great China Restaurant, Capitol Theatre, Chinese Post Office,
Astor House and Palace Hotels. He has also paid visits to the
pages.zh:
D 828
1930年5月21日

W.O. Allen 于4月11日中午12点乘“Angers”号轮船
从香港抵达上海。他在四川路海军青年会住宿一晚，
次日即4月12日搬至中华基督教青年会，入住16号房间。

据悉，他在上海逗留期间，曾与一名名为 Erappa 的印度人接触，
此人此前与南京路的《字林西报》有关联，已知他们
于5月2日访问了宝山路（Paoshan Road）的印度谒师所。
当日，Allen 和 Erappa 会见了两名印度人（锡克教徒），
其中一人在博物馆路10号担任看守。他们之间传递并
查看了文件，随后进行了热烈的交谈。

Allen 还与几名住在斯科特路第二弄堂的中國学生有联系。
这些中国人可能在中华基督教青年会学习。他还经常
被人看见与两名居住在巨鹿路2089号的中国人在一起。
他们的姓名等目前尚不清楚，但正在进行调查以确认
其身份。

他曾多次被人看见与两名日本人在一起，他经常在
四川路188号的大中华餐厅与这两名日本人会面。
这两名日本人常去南京路的东方饭店，并已知在福州路
的一家中国餐馆与学生模样的中国人会面。在该餐馆
见到的一名中国人会说日语。

汪智廣（Wang Chi-Kwang），芜湖人，也曾被人看见
与 Allen 在一起。此人是上海学院毕业生，目前在该校
担任会计。他有一个兄弟在美国东方贸易公司任职。

Allen 经常出入的场所如下：海军青年会、
大中华餐厅、卡德大戏院（Capitol Theatre）、华邮局、
礼查饭店（Astor House）和华懋饭店（Palace Hotels）。他还曾造访

pages.en:
- 2 -

North Railway Station and to the Postal Remittance and Savings
Bank, No. 5 Foochow Road. It is believed that he made an
unsuccessful attempt to cash a cheque at this place.
On May 24th Allen removed to the Hongkew Hotel, North
Szechuen Road, where he occupied room No. 147 with his wife,
who is believed to have arrived in Shanghai the previous day.
On June 1st he and his wife left for Nanking and resided at
the Central Hotel ( Chinese ) until 10 p.m. June 3rd, when
they left for Hangchow. During Allen's visit to Nanking he
is known to have paid two visits to the offices of the Far
Eastern Oppressed People's Association. The purpose of their
visit to Hangchow is unknown, but while there they resided
at the "West Lake" Hotel, returning to Shanghai on June 6th.
On June 9th they both left for Tientsin/3rd Class on the S.S.
"Tientsin Maru."
pages.zh:
- 2 -

北站以及福州路5号的邮政储金汇业局。
据信他曾试图在此兑现一张支票但未成功。
5月24日，Allen 搬至北四川路的虹口大酒店，
与其妻子同住147号房间，据信其妻于前一日抵沪。
6月1日，他和妻子前往南京，入住中央饭店（华人经营），
直至6月3日晚上10点离开前往杭州。已知 Allen 在
南京期间曾两次拜访远东被压迫民族协会办事处。
他们前往杭州的目的不明，但在杭州期间他们入住
“西湖”饭店，并于6月6日返回上海。
6月9日，两人乘坐“天津丸”号轮船三等舱前往天津。

May 15th. At 11.5 a.m. Allen left the Chinese Y.M.C.A.,
put on sun glasses and walked along Szechuen
Road to Hankow Road, returned to Kiukiang
Road, stayed little while on the corner,
carefully observing the vicinity, then walked
along to the Bund, and entered the H. & S.
Bank, stayed in the Hall for about 10 minutes,
then walked out through the Foochow Road
entrance, quickly got into a ricsha and
proceeded along Foochow, Szechuen, Canton
Roads, then along the Bund and returned back
to Foochow Road. It was then 11.45 a.m.
He then entered the Postal Remittance &
Savings Bank, No. 5 Foochow Road, where he
produced a cheque (of a pink colour) to a
clerk, who did not cash it and returned the
cheque to Allen. They conversed for a few
minutes and Allen then left the Bank, got
into a ricsha and proceeded along Szechuen
Road, Nanking Road, along the Bund, along
Soochow, and Hongkong Roads. He then entered
the Navy Y.M.C.A., ordered a cup of coffee,
and after a little while returned to the
Y.M.C.A.
At 4.5 p.m. Allen was seen returning to the
Chinese Y.M.C.A. in company with a Chinese
student, who was mentioned in previous reports,
as having visited St. John's University,
Jessfield Road, and who resides off Scott Road.

May 14th. Watch was commenced at 12.30 p.m.
At 6.20 p.m. Allen left the Y.M.C.A. and
walked along Chapoo Road Bridge to the
General Post Office, where he bought several
stamps and posted a few letters. He then
walked to the Capitol Theatre where he remained
until 8.55 p.m. On leaving the Theatre,
Allen walked into the Great China Restaurant,
188 Szechuen Road, where he ordered a cup of
coffee and some cakes.
At 9.5 p.m. a Japanese (who was mentioned in
the previous report, as having met Allen in
the same Restaurant) entered the and sat down
at Allen's table. They conversed until 9.35 p.m.
when the Japanese left the Restaurant and
walked to the General Post Office, where he
got into a ricksha and proceeded to Peking
Road Jetty, where he paid off his ricksha.
He then walked to the Customs House and then to
Nanking Road and the Bund corner. Here he
boarded Omnibus No. 1, and proceeded to Thibet
Road, where he alighted, got into a ricksha
and proceeded to the Great Eastern Hotel,
Thibet Road, which he entered and remained
there until 10.35 p.m. He then walked to the
Grand Hotel, Thibet Road, where he remained
until 10.55 p.m. after which he proceeded by
ricksha to the Oriental Hotel, Nanking Road.
The agent then returned to the Y.M.C.A. and

May 12th. At 2.45 p.m. Allen left the Y.M.C.A. and
walked to the Navy Y.M.C.A., where he remained
until 3.20 p.m., and then returned to the
Y.M.C.A.
At 6.00 p.m. he left the Y.M.C.A. in company
with two persons who appeared to be natives
of Annam or the Malay States. Their description
is as follows:- 1st, aged about 25 years,
medium height, rather stout build, fat round
face, no hat, black suit, patent leather shoes.
2nd, aged about 20 years, medium height, thin
build, thin face, no hat, black suit, black
shoes with white lines on them. These two
persons walked to the Navy Y.M.C.A., while
Allen walked to the Capitol Theatre. Allen
remained there for little while, then came out,
got into a ricksha and proceeded to Chapoo
Road where he entered the Hongkew Theatre.
At 8.00 p.m. Allen left the Hongkew Theatre,
and walked along Haining Road to North Szechuen
Road, where he got into a ricksha, and proceeded
along Range Road to the North Railway Station,
where he met one of the Railway employees,
with whom he spoke in Chinese. They conversed
for about 15 minutes, then Allen got into his
ricksha and proceeded along North Szechuen Road
to the General Post Office where he paid off
his ricksha and walked to the Y.M.C.A. It was
then 9.45 p.m.

May 11th. At 5.35 p.m. 2 Indians departed from the
Chinese Y.M.C.A. Their description is as
under:- (1st) Aged about 35 years, of medium
height and stout build, has round face
with a small black moustache, was wearing
grey hat, grey overcoat, black trousers
and new brown shoes. (2nd) Aged about 30
years, tall, thin build, has thin long
face and is clean shaven, was wearing dark
grey hat, blue serge jacket, grey trousers
and brown shoes, and carrying a walking
stick, and a black leather portfolio.
These two men engaged rickshas and proceeded
via North Szechien Road to the Gurdwara on
Paoshan Road, Chapei, where they remained
for about 20 minutes. Engaging rickshas they
then proceeded direct to the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
at which place they arrived at 6.40 p.m.

institution in rickshas and proceeded to an
alleyway off Kunping Road between East
Seward and Tonshan Roads. Owing to the
large number of Indians standing near the
mouth of the alleyway, the agent was unable
to ascertain the number of the house visited
by the two men he was following.

William Dangaik Allen alias William Dangaise alias William

He resided for one day at the Navy Y.M.C.A. and the following
day, April 12th, he removed to the Chinese Y.M.C.A., Szechuen
Road, where he now occupies Room No. 16.
Since his arrival observation has been kept on his movements.
Nothing of much importance occurred until May 2nd prior to
which his movements generally consisted of visits to the
American Consulate, Post Office, Navy Y.M.C.A., Astor and
Palace Hotels. At 4.30 p.m. April 23rd he visited H.B.M.
Consulate where he proceeded upstairs and remained for 20
minutes.

clean shaven, very dark face, wearing glasses, dressed in
European light brown clothes, grey turban and brown shoes.
Allen and this Indian entered into conversation and walked
together along as far as Tiendong Road and Szechuen Road corner.

showed to Allen. After reading the papers, Allen tapped the
Indian on the shoulder and seemed to be impressing something
on him. They then walked to Szechuen and Haining Roads corner,
where they met two other Indians, dressed in watchman uniform.
One of them is employed at No. 15 Museum Road. All entered
into conversation and the papers previously shown to Allen
were again examined, after which they walked South along
North Szechuen Road for a little way, when the two Indians met
at Haining Road left Allen and his companion, who got into

先生，

威廉·丹盖克·艾伦，又名威廉·丹盖斯，又名威廉·艾伦，于4月11日乘“昂热”号（s.s. "Angers"）轮船抵达上海。他在海军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.）居住了一天，次日即4月12日，搬至四川路中华基督教青年会（Chinese Y.M.C.A.），目前居住在16号房间。

自其抵达以来，一直对其行踪进行监视。在5月2日之前未发生什么重要情况，在此期间他的活动主要包括访问美国领事馆、邮局、海军青年会、阿斯特酒店（Astor Hotel）和宫殿酒店（Palace Hotel）。4月23日下午4时30分，他访问了英国驻华领事馆（H.B.M. Consulate），随后上楼并停留了20分钟。

Precis.

William Dangalk Allen, alias William Dangaiae, alias
William Daugaix, suspected Communist, is stated to be an
American journalist, a student of International relations and
to be the son of Dr. W. h. Allen of New York City.
His description is as follows:-
26/27 years of age, tall, slim,
clean-shaven and wearing spectacles.
He is reported to speak French and German fluently and to
have a slight knowledge of Italian and Spanish. For the past
three years Allen has been travelling in Europe and arrived in
India about July, 1929, where he taught English in Dr. R. N.
Tagore's Santiniketan, Bolpur. He was interested in the Youth
Movement, and whilst in Calcutta attended, in Khaddar clothes,
the recent Congress of the North Calcutta District Youth
Association. In connection with his visit to the Far East, he
visited the Kuomintang Representative in Calcutta to ascertain
the cost of living in China. It is stated that he wished to
study the question of the Singapore base and local mineral
resources there.
He is in possession of a third class passage from France
to Shanghai, which is valid for two years.
He left Colombo on the 27th January for Singapore, where
he stayed for three days, leaving for Bangkok on the 4th January,
which journey he made overland. Whilst in Singapore he was
under surveillance, but his movements disclosed nothing suspicious.
He arrived in Hong Kong from Saigon on the 26th February
last, per s.s. "Chenonceaux". On 27.2.30. he left instructions
with the American Consulate, Hong Kong, to forward all mail, c/o
Post Restante, Manila. The name of W. Allen was shown as a 3rd
class passenger from Manila to Hong Kong on the s.s. "Empress of
Russia", arriving 6.4.30, but no trace of his going there can be
found. He left for Shanghai on 8th April per s.s. "Angers"
leaving instructions for future mail to be forwarded to the
American Consulate, Shanghai.

摘要。

威廉·丹加尔克·艾伦（William Dangalk Allen），又名威廉·丹加埃（William Dangaiae），又名威廉·杜盖克斯（William Daugaix），疑似共产主义者，据称是一名美国记者，国际关系学者，系纽约市 W. H. 艾伦博士之子。
其体貌特征如下：-
年龄26/27岁，身材高大，消瘦，面部光洁无须，戴眼镜。
据报他能流利说法语和德语，并略懂意大利语和西班牙语。过去三年，艾伦一直在欧洲旅行，于1929年7月左右抵达印度，在博尔普尔（Bolpur）的圣蒂尼克坦（Santiniketan）R. N. 泰戈尔博士处教授英语。他对青年运动感兴趣，在加尔各答期间，身着卡迪（Khaddar）服装，参加了北加尔各答区青年协会最近的代表大会。就其远东之行而言，他曾拜访国民党驻加尔各答代表，以了解中国的生活费用。据称，他希望研究新加坡基地及当地矿产资源的问题。
他持有一张从法国到上海的三等舱船票，有效期为两年。
他于1月27日离开科伦坡前往新加坡，在那里停留了三天，随后于1月4日前往曼谷，该段旅程为陆路。（注：原文日期逻辑有误，1月27日离科伦坡，1月4日去曼谷，时间倒置，此处照实翻译）。在新加坡期间，他受到监视，但其行踪未显示任何可疑之处。
他于去年2月26日乘“谢农索号”（s.s. "Chenonceaux"）轮船从西贡抵达香港。1930年2月27日，他指示美国驻香港领事馆将所有邮件转交至马尼拉邮政待领处（Post Restante, Manila）。“W. Allen”的名字曾作为三等舱乘客出现在从马尼拉前往香港的“俄罗斯皇后号”（s.s. "Empress of Russia"）轮船上，该船于1930年4月6日抵达，但查无此人前往该地的记录。他于4月8日乘“昂热号”（s.s. "Angers"）轮船前往上海，并指示将后续邮件转交至美国驻上海领事馆。

Allen at that time visited several exchange shops and the
Navy Y.M.C.A. restaurant with a Chinese. As it is impossible
to continually supervise them there is a possibility that
such lapses will occur in the future and we would therefore
be unable to keep a proper check on Allen's movements.

Two agents are meantime employed from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
and from 3 to 9 p.m. at a cost of $1.00 each per day. A
Russian agent could be employed at $2.00 per day and would
do duty of 9 hours per day. Any additional supervision on
Allen's movements could be carried out by detectives attached
to this Section.

In this manner I am sure far more reliable information
could be obtained.

My dear Aiers,

Many thanks for your letter No.I-O- D.828 of
April 2nd 1930, on the subject of W.D.ALLEN. A recently inter-
cepted letter written by him, copy of which I received from India,
contained the following: "When I imagine to myself more carefully
"the physical difficulties of such a project re China as I have been
"talking on, I am aghast. Not as to permanent conditions but I have
"had the hope of doing the whole starting while you were there. But
"as I must apparently know a smattering of Chinese and know a lot
"about Chinese and Europeans to be met, before I could launch the
"thing seriously, I fear you wont see much actually done while you
are there"

I do not know what it is he proposes to launch, but it
is fairly clear that he intends to visit China sooner or later.

Yours sincerely,

A.D.Blackburn

R.C.Aiers, Esq.,
Director of Criminal Investigation,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

Sir,

I have the honour to request that you will
kindly send me any information in your possession
regarding an alleged Communist named William Dangauk
Allen, who, according to a report made to us, visited
Hongkong in February 1930.

William Dangauk Allen, who is a journalist by
profession, is reported to be a son of Dr. W.H. Allen
of New York City. After having travelled for some time
in India, he departed in the early part of 1930 for
the Far East. He first visited Singapore and afterwards
Indo-China. He proceeded from the latter place by the
s.s. "Chenonceaux" to Hongkong, where he arrived on
February 26, 1930.

Allen is tall, slim, clean shaven and is said
to be 26 or 27 years old.

Any particulars about him, which you be good
enough to send me, will be greatly appreciated.

SECRET

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No I. O. D. 828.
H.B.M. Consul-General,
Shanghai,
31st December 1929.

My dear Aiers,

I have received information from India that a suspected Communist named William Dangaik Allen recently came to notice in Calcutta. He is stated to be an American journalist, a student of International relations and a son of Dr W.H.Allen of New York City. He is reported to speak French and German fluently and to have a slight knowledge of Italian and Spanish. He arrived in India from Europe about August 1929 and has been taking an interest in political movements. In connection with his visit to the Far East he paid a visit to the Kuomintang representative in Calcutta by whom he was recommended to write to Ganda Singh, the secretary of the Eastern Oppressed Peoples Association at Nanking. After attending the Indian National Conference at Lahore, he proposes to leave India for China via Colombo about the end of January 1930, staying at Singapore, Hongkong and in Indo-China en route. His description is as follows:-

26/27 years of age, tall, slim, clean shaven, wearing spectacles.

There is some possibility that Allen may be identical with the C.P.Leader referred to in the correspondence ending with your letter No D 528 of the 20th November 1929.

Yours sincerely,

G.H.A. Hallam.

R.C.Aiers Esq.,
Director of Criminal Investigation,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Foreign Section
For careful inquiry and report
please.
G.H.A. 3/1/30

亲爱的艾尔斯（Aiers）：

我从印度收到消息，一名名为 William Dangaik Allen 的涉嫌共产主义者最近在加尔各答引起注意。据称他是一名美国记者，国际关系学者，也是纽约市 W.H. Allen 博士之子。据报他能流利说法语和德语，并略通意大利语和西班牙语。他于1929年8月左右从欧洲抵达印度，一直对政治运动感兴趣。在他访问远东之际，他拜访了加尔各答的国民党代表，该代表推荐他写信给南京东方被压迫民族协会秘书甘达·辛格（Ganda Singh）。在参加拉合尔的印度国民会议后，他计划于1930年1月底左右经科伦坡离开印度前往中国，途中停留新加坡、香港和印度支那。他的体貌特征如下：-

26/27岁，身材高大，瘦削，面部光洁无胡须，戴眼镜。

Allen 有可能与您1929年11月20日第 D 528 号来信为止的通信中提到的共产党领导人系同一人。

此致
敬礼，

G.H.A. 哈勒姆（Hallam）。

刑事侦缉处处长，
上海公共租界工部局。
